examples.ko: 이 사안은 대표님께 먼저 보고해야 해요.
examples.en: This matter has to be reported to the CEO first.

examples.ko: 중요한 사안이라서 회의를 다시 열기로 했어요.
examples.en: It is an important matter, so we decided to hold another meeting.
Everyone knows how serious the issue is.

examples.ko: 법원이 이번 사안을 조심스럽게 검토하고 있어요.
examples.en: The court is carefully reviewing this case.
Keep a record even of a small matter.

examples.ko: 두 가지 사안을 따로 다루면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: It would be good to handle the two issues separately.

explain: 사안은 회의나 법원, 뉴스에서 다루는 일이나 문제를 가리켜요. 일상에서는 '일'이나 '문제'가 더 자연스러워요. 보통 '중요한 사안', '민감한 사안'처럼 꾸밈말이 앞에 와요.

phrases.en: Politics is a sensitive matter, so I'm careful what I say.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조심스럽게 다뤄야 하는 문제를 말할 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical phrase for an issue that must be handled carefully.

phrases.en: The matter is serious, so the police are investigating.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제가 크고 중요하다는 것을 서술어와 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses a predicate to say that the issue is big and important.

phrases.en: We decided to review each case separately.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-별로'를 붙여 문제마다 하나씩 나눠서 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -별로 means looking at each issue one by one.

explain_en: A matter or item to be handled, esp. meetings and news. 사안 refers to a matter dealt with in meetings, courts or the news. In daily talk 일 or 문제 is more natural. It usually has a modifier before it, as in '중요한 사안' (important matter) or '민감한 사안' (sensitive matter).

en: to be inherited; to be succeeded

examples.en: The house was passed down to the son.
The property is inherited equally by the children.
When the company passed to his daughter, its name changed.

examples.ko: 유언이 없으면 재산은 법에 따라 상속될 거예요.
examples.en: Without a will, the property will be inherited according to law.

examples.ko: 이 땅은 오래전에 할아버지께 상속된 거예요.
examples.en: This land was inherited from my grandfather long ago.
Tax is charged on inherited property.

explain: 상속되다는 재산이나 권리가 법에 따라 사람에게서 사람에게 넘어갈 때 써서 집, 땅, 회사 같은 대상과 함께 나와요. 성격이나 얼굴이 닮는 것은 '유전되다', 전통이 이어지는 것은 '전해지다'라고 해요. 받는 사람 쪽은 '상속받다'를 써요.

phrases.en: My grandfather's estate was passed on to the family.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유산'은 돌아가신 분이 남긴 재산으로 '상속'과 자주 함께 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: '유산' is the property left behind and often appears with '상속'.

phrases.en: This land will be passed on to my daughter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 일어날 일을 말할 때 쓰는 미래 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A future form for something that will happen.

phrases.en: I inherited the shop from my father.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받는 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy word used when the recipient is the subject.

explain_en: Passive; property or rights are passed to someone (집이 상속되다) 상속되다 is for property or rights passing legally from one person to another, so it goes with houses, land and companies. Looks and personality passed on are 유전되다, and traditions handed down are 전해지다. From the receiver's side you say 상속받다.

t90.ax: The house was passed down to the son.

examples.en: I got tax documents at the tax office.
You have to go to the tax office to register a business.
The tax office opens at nine on weekdays.
The tax office is close to my home.
A tax office employee explained kindly.
I have to send the documents to the tax office.

explain: 세무서는 세금을 걷고 신고를 받는 곳이에요. 신고를 대신해 주는 사람은 '세무사'라서 서로 달라요. 요즘은 '홈택스'로 인터넷에서도 신고해요. 주소나 증명서 일은 '구청'이나 '주민센터'에서 해요.

phrases.en: I'm going to the tax office for business registration.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금 일을 하러 간다고 말할 때 가장 기본으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic way to say you go for tax matters.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to the tax office

phrases.en: If you have income, you must report it to the tax office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금과 관련된 내용을 공식적으로 알린다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means officially reporting tax-related information.
phrases.en_equiv: to report to the tax office

phrases.en: A tax office employee checked the documents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세무서에서 일하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who works at the tax office.

explain_en: 세무서 is where taxes are collected and returns are filed. The person who files for you is a 세무사, which is different. These days people also file online through 홈택스. Address and certificate matters go to the 구청 or 주민센터.

en: to apply retroactively; to trace back

examples.en: The new law applies retroactively back to last month.
I received the raised salary retroactively back to March.

examples.ko: 이 규정을 과거 사건에 소급하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You can't apply this rule retroactively to past cases.

examples.ko: 환불 규정을 소급할 수 있는지 문의했어요.
examples.en: I asked whether the refund policy can be applied retroactively.

examples.ko: 소급하는 방식에 대해 직원들의 의견이 갈렸어요.
examples.en: Employees' opinions were divided on the retroactive approach.
The company decided not to apply the compensation retroactively.

explain: 법, 규정, 금액 같은 것이 지나간 시점까지 거슬러 올라가 적용될 때 써요. 보통 '소급 적용'이라는 말로 많이 들리고, 월급 인상이나 새 규정 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '거슬러 올라가다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: This rule applies retroactively from January of this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지나간 때까지 거슬러 적용한다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase, meaning applied back to a past date.

phrases.example: 오른 월급을 두 달 치 소급해서 받았어요.
phrases.en: I received the raised salary retroactively for two months.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 지난 기간의 돈을 나중에 한꺼번에 받을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when receiving money for a past period afterwards.

phrases.example: 이 이야기는 백 년 전으로 거슬러 올라가요.
phrases.en: This story goes back a hundred years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 과거로 돌아간다고 말할 때 쓰는 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday expression for going back to the past.

explain_en: To go back to an earlier time, as in records or laws. It is used when a law, rule or amount is applied going back to an earlier point in time. You often hear it as '소급 적용', especially in talk of pay raises or new regulations. In daily speech, people also say '거슬러 올라가다'.

t90.ax: The new law applies retroactively back to last month.

examples.en: The court sent a summons notice to the witness.
He answered the prosecutors' summons.
In the game, I learned a monster summoning skill.

examples.ko: 소환 날짜가 바뀌어서 일정을 다시 잡았어요.
examples.en: The summons date changed, so I rescheduled.
The news said the ambassador had been recalled to his home country.

examples.ko: 소환에 응하지 않으면 체포될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you don't comply with the summons, you can be arrested.

explain: 법원이나 검찰이 사람을 정해진 곳으로 부를 때 쓰는 공식적인 말이에요. 일상에서 '부르다'는 아무나 쓰지만 소환은 공식 기관이 쓸 때 가장 자연스러워요. 요즘은 게임에서 캐릭터를 불러올 때도 '소환'이라고 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: A summons came from the court.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소환을 알리는 공식 문서를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The official document that announces a summons.

phrases.en: He answered the prosecutors' summons.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부름을 받고 실제로 간다는 뜻의 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation meaning one actually goes when summoned.

phrases.en: He was summoned to court as a witness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부름을 받는 사람을 주어로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the person being summoned as the subject.

explain_en: The act of summoning someone to court or an office; the process itself, formal. It is the official word for a court or prosecutor calling a person to a set place. Anyone can use '부르다' in daily life, but 소환 is most natural from an official body. These days it is also widely used in games for calling up characters.

examples.en: A summons arrived from the court yesterday.

examples.ko: 소환장을 받으면 정해진 날짜에 출석해야 해요.
examples.en: If you receive a summons, you must appear on the set date.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 소환장을 무시하고 나타나지 않았어요.
examples.en: He ignored the summons and did not show up.
They say the police sent a summons to the witness.

examples.ko: 우편함에 소환장 같은 서류가 들어 있어서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised to find a document like a summons in the mailbox.

examples.ko: 소환장에 적힌 시간에 맞춰 법원에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the court at the time written on the summons.

explain: '소환장을 받다/보내다/발부하다'처럼 써요. 법원이나 검찰에서 오는 공식 서류라서 일상 대화보다 뉴스에 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: I received a summons by mail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법원 등에서 오는 소환 서류를 받았을 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for receiving an official summons from a court or similar body.

phrases.en: The court sent a summons to the witness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기관이 사람에게 출석하라고 서류를 보낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an institution sends a document ordering someone to appear.

phrases.en: Once the summons was issued, he decided to appear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식적으로 소환장이 만들어져 나왔다는 뜻이며 뉴스에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a summons was officially issued, and is common in news reports.

explain_en: The written summons document itself, the notice that is sent (소환). It is used in phrases like '소환장을 받다/보내다/발부하다'. Because it is an official document from a court or prosecutors' office, you meet it more in the news than in daily talk.

t90.ax: A summons arrived from the court yesterday.

examples.en: The court summoned the witness.
The police will summon that person.
A summons letter came to my house.
I summon a new character in the game.
The National Assembly decided to summon the CEO.

examples.ko: 그 마법사는 불의 정령을 소환하려고 주문을 외웠어요.
examples.en: The wizard recited a spell to summon a fire spirit.

explain: 수사나 재판에서 사람을 불러 오게 할 때 '소환하다'를 써요. 일상에서 사람을 부를 때는 '부르다'를 써요. 게임이나 판타지에서 캐릭터를 불러낼 때도 '소환하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The witness was summoned to court.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소환하다'의 피동형으로, 불려 가는 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, used when the person being summoned is the subject.

phrases.en: A summons came to my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법원이나 경찰이 보내는 부르는 문서를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The official paper sent by a court or police to summon someone.

phrases.en: I summon a character in the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임이나 판타지에서 불러낼 때 쓰는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Usage in games and fantasy for calling something forth.

explain_en: In investigations and trials, it is the verb for ordering someone to appear. In daily life you just use '부르다' (call). It is also used for calling up characters in games and fantasy stories.

examples.en: Thanks to the lawyer, we won the trial.

examples.ko: 이번 승소는 회사에 큰 도움이 됐어요.
examples.en: This court win was a big help to the company.
Everyone was happy to hear the news of the win in court.
The chance that we will win the case is not high.
If you win the case, you can receive compensation.

examples.ko: 작은 가게가 대기업과의 소송에서 승소를 거뒀어요.
examples.en: A small shop won its lawsuit against a large corporation.

explain: 반대말은 '패소'예요. 소송이나 재판에서만 써서 일상 대화에서는 드물고, 뉴스에서 '~이 승소했다'로 자주 들려요. 시합이나 게임에서 이기는 건 '이기다', '승리하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Our side won the lawsuit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '승소'에 '하다'를 붙인 동사로, 소송에서 이겼다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, meaning to win in a lawsuit.

phrases.example: 법원이 회사 쪽에 승소 판결을 내렸어요.
phrases.en: The court ruled in favor of the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법원이 이긴 쪽을 정해 주는 결정을 말해요. 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The court's decision naming the winning side. Often heard in the news.

phrases.en: That lawyer has a high win rate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소송에서 이긴 비율을 말할 때 변호사 이야기에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The share of cases won. Often used when talking about lawyers.

explain_en: The opposite is 패소. It is used only for lawsuits and trials, so it is rare in everyday talk, but you often hear '~이 승소했다' in the news. For winning a match or a game, use 이기다 or 승리하다.

examples.en: The police search and seizure began in the morning.
Confiscated items are kept in a warehouse.
Items that were seized are hard to get back.

examples.ko: 시험 중 휴대전화 압수는 학교 규칙이에요.
examples.en: Confiscating phones during exams is a school rule.
The shop owner was flustered by the sudden seizure.
Seizures of illegal copies are increasing.

explain: 압수는 경찰이나 학교처럼 권한이 있는 쪽이 물건을 가져가는 일이에요. 뉴스에서는 '압수 수색'이라고 한 덩어리로 자주 나와요. 훔치는 것과 달리 법이나 규칙에 따라 가져간다는 점이 달라요.

phrases.en: The police got a seizure warrant from the court.
phrases.nuance_ko: 압수를 해도 된다는 법원의 허락 문서예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A court document that allows seizure.

phrases.en: At the airport, confiscated items are stored separately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 압수된 물건 자체를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the items that were confiscated.

phrases.example: 수업 중에 쓰다가 제 휴대폰이 압수됐어요.
phrases.en: My phone was confiscated when I used it in class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 가져가진 쪽에서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the item that was taken away.

explain_en: Authority or teacher takes items; police evidence, banned things. 압수 is used when someone with authority, such as the police or a school, takes an item away. In the news it often appears as the set phrase 압수 수색. Unlike stealing, it is done under a law or rule.

examples.en: The teacher confiscated the game console during class.
Customs confiscated the fruit in the bag.

examples.ko: 규칙을 어기면 물건을 압수할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you break the rules, your things can be confiscated.
The police seized the computer and investigated.
They give back confiscated items later.

examples.ko: 부모님이 제 휴대폰을 압수해서 연락을 못 했어요.
examples.en: My parents took my phone away, so I couldn't get in touch.

explain: '압수하다'는 가져가는 사람이 경찰, 세관, 선생님처럼 권한이 있는 사람이에요. 친구끼리 장난으로 뺏을 때는 '뺏다'를 써요. 뺏기는 쪽은 '압수당하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: My comic book was confiscated during class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 뺏기는 사람의 입장에서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the viewpoint of the person whose item is taken.

phrases.en: The police confiscated the documents and took them away.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 가다'를 붙여 물건을 가지고 간다는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-아/어 가다' adds the sense of taking the item away.

phrases.en: This time the teacher did not confiscate the phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 압수가 일어나지 않았다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says no confiscation happened.

explain_en: The one doing 압수하다 is someone with authority, such as the police, customs, or a teacher. When friends take something playfully, they use 뺏다. The person it is taken from says 압수당하다.

examples.ko: 이혼할 때 아이의 양육권을 누가 갖는지 정해야 해요.
examples.en: When parents divorce, they have to decide who gets custody of the child.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 양육권 문제로 오래 다퉜어요.
examples.en: The two of them argued for a long time over the custody issue.
The court granted custody to the mother.
Can the father also demand custody?
A custody lawsuit takes a long time.

examples.ko: 아이가 클 때까지 양육권은 엄마가 가지기로 했어요.
examples.en: They decided that the mother would have custody until the child grows up.

explain: 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 '이혼', '친권', '소송'과 같이 자주 나와요. 보통 '양육권을 갖다', '양육권을 얻다', '양육권을 주장하다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: The mother ended up getting custody of the child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재판이나 합의로 아이를 키울 권리를 얻었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means gaining the right to raise the child through a court ruling or agreement.

phrases.en: The father also claimed custody.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 아이를 키우겠다고 말하는 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when both sides say they want to raise the child.

phrases.example: 양육권 소송이 일 년 넘게 이어졌어요.
phrases.en: The custody lawsuit went on for over a year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양육권 때문에 법원에서 다투는 일을 말하고, 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A court dispute over custody; common in the news.

explain_en: It often appears in news and legal talk together with words like '이혼' (divorce), '친권' (parental authority) and '소송' (lawsuit). It is usually used as '양육권을 갖다', '양육권을 얻다' or '양육권을 주장하다'.

examples.ko: 시민들은 사기 범죄에 대한 엄벌을 요구했어요.
examples.en: Citizens demanded severe punishment for fraud.

examples.ko: 이런 범죄는 엄벌에 처해야 한다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think crimes like this should be severely punished.

examples.ko: 엄벌만이 해결책은 아니라고 말하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people say that harsh punishment alone is not the solution.

examples.ko: 정부는 개인 정보를 판 업체에 엄벌 방침을 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The government announced a policy of severe punishment for companies that sold personal data.

examples.ko: 판결이 나오자 엄벌을 바라던 가족들이 눈물을 흘렸어요.
examples.en: When the verdict came out, the families who had hoped for harsh punishment cried.

examples.ko: 회사 비밀을 지키지 않으면 엄벌이 따라요.
examples.en: If you don't keep company secrets, severe punishment follows.

explain: 뉴스와 판결 이야기에서 '엄벌에 처하다', '엄벌을 요구하다'처럼 자주 나와요. 반대되는 느낌의 말은 '선처'예요.

phrases.en: The court imposed a severe punishment on the criminal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스와 판결 이야기에서 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation in news and court reports.

phrases.example: 정부는 불법 행위에 엄벌을 내리겠다고 했어요.
phrases.en: The government said it would impose severe punishment on illegal acts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권한 있는 쪽이 강한 처벌을 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an authority decides on a harsh punishment.

phrases.en: Citizens urged severe punishment for the offender.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강한 처벌을 하라고 강하게 요구할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when strongly calling for harsh punishment.

explain_en: Severe punishment for serious crimes — news, courts (엄벌에 처하다) It appears often in news and court stories in phrases like '엄벌에 처하다' and '엄벌을 요구하다'. A word with the opposite feeling is '선처' (leniency).

examples.ko: 정부는 불법 행위를 엄중히 처벌하겠다고 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The government said it will punish illegal acts severely.

examples.ko: 회사는 이번 일을 엄중히 다루고 있어요.
examples.en: The company is handling this matter very seriously.

examples.ko: 선생님이 시험 중 부정행위를 엄중히 경고하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher sternly warned against cheating during the exam.

examples.ko: 경찰이 엄중히 경계하는 가운데 행사가 열렸어요.
examples.en: The event took place under tight security by the police.

examples.ko: 규칙을 어긴 사람에게 엄중히 책임을 묻기로 했어요.
examples.en: They decided to hold those who broke the rules strictly responsible.
This problem has to be taken very seriously.

explain: '엄하게'와 비슷하지만 뉴스, 공문, 공식 발표에서 '엄중히 경고하다/처벌하다/대응하다'처럼 더 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서 혼내는 상황에는 '엄하게', '따끔하게'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The police sternly warned the drivers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 공식 발표에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in news and official announcements.

phrases.example: 학교는 폭력 문제에 엄중히 대응하기로 했어요.
phrases.en: The school decided to respond strictly to the violence issue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제나 잘못에 단호하게 맞서는 공식적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal expression for dealing firmly with a problem or wrongdoing.

phrases.en: My father speaks sternly when I break a promise.
phrases.nuance_ko: '엄중히'보다 일상적이라 혼내거나 가르치는 상황에 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More everyday than '엄중히'; natural for scolding or teaching.

explain_en: Formal; firm, serious handling of rules or punishment (엄중히 경고하다) It is similar to '엄하게', but it shows up more in news, official documents and announcements, as in '엄중히 경고하다', '처벌하다' and '대응하다'. For scolding someone in daily life, '엄하게' or '따끔하게' sounds more natural.

t90.ax: This problem has to be taken very seriously.

examples.ko: 이사장이 한 번 더 연임하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The chairman decided to serve one more consecutive term.

examples.ko: 그 회사의 대표는 세 번이나 연임했어요.
examples.en: That company's CEO served three consecutive terms.

examples.ko: 이 단체의 회장은 연임할 수 없어요.
examples.en: The head of this organization cannot serve consecutive terms.
To serve another term, you need approval from the shareholders' meeting.

examples.ko: 시장이 연임해서 도시 계획이 계속 이어질 거예요.
examples.en: The mayor is serving another term, so the city plan will continue.

examples.ko: 원래 연임하는 사람이 드물어서 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: People who serve consecutive terms are rare, so it became a talking point.

explain: 주어가 그 직책을 맡는 사람이고, '대표가 연임하다'처럼 써요. 선거나 승인을 거쳐 다음 임기를 이어서 맡는 느낌이에요. 뉴스에서는 '연임에 성공하다'처럼 명사 형태도 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: The association president succeeded in being re-elected.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 명사 '연임'과 함께 자주 나오는 짝이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A frequent news pairing with the noun '연임'.
phrases.en_equiv: to succeed in serving another term

phrases.example: 이 자리는 한 번만 연임할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can serve only one more consecutive term in this post.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄹ 수 있다'로 가능한 횟수나 조건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses '-ㄹ 수 있다' to state what is allowed.

phrases.en: He was reappointed as CEO for another consecutive term.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람의 결정으로 다음 임기를 이어서 맡게 됐을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when one is kept on for the next term by others' decision.

explain_en: The subject is the person holding the post, as in '대표가 연임하다'. It feels like continuing into the next term after an election or approval. In the news the noun form also appears a lot, such as '연임에 성공하다'.
